sources.title: Jinchao Xu, Iterative Methods by Space Decomposition and Subspace Correction, SIAM Review 34(4) (1992)
sources.locator: Complete 34-page paper inspected; §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 585–588, §4.1 and the opening of §4.2, printed pp. 591–594. The source supplies abstract subspace-correction, additive-spectrum, and ordered-sweep arguments.

contents.name: §3.1, space decompositions and restricted subspace equations (3.1)–(3.3)
contents.reason: The carrier gives the finite-dimensional restriction and prolongation conventions explicitly, then its local lemma checks the restricted SPD matrices.

contents.name: §3.2, parallel subspace correction, additive operator (3.6), and Lemma 3.1
contents.reason: The source identifies the additive inverse as a sum of local restricted inverses; the local carrier proves every term exists under its stated full-rank hypotheses.

contents.name: §3.3, successive subspace correction and ordered error products (3.8)
contents.reason: The local theorem derives its ordered product and contraction by its own energy telescoping proof, consistent with the source route.

contents.name: §4.1, Theorem 4.1 (Fundamental Theorem I), additive spectrum from stable splitting and synthesis
contents.reason: The local theorem proves both Rayleigh bounds directly and additionally derives the inexact local-solver comparison.

contents.name: §4.1, Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 4.4 (Fundamental Theorem II), multiplicative energy decrease
contents.reason: The item gives a full ordered projection proof with explicit C0, C1, and overlap-norm constants.

contents.name: Opening §4.2, Lemmas 4.5–4.7 and strengthened Cauchy–Schwarz overlap estimates
contents.reason: The item states its overlap matrix hypothesis and proves the finite-matrix norm estimate used to bound the ordered sweep.

contents.name: §3.1–§3.2 examples of scalar and point/block subspace decompositions
contents.reason: The example independently computes the exact one-dimensional point-patch spectrum and its divergence with mesh size.

sources.title: Peter Bastian, Lecture Notes on Parallel Solution of Large Sparse Linear Systems, University of Heidelberg (2015)
sources.locator: Complete 154-page lecture notes inspected; Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.4, printed pp. 37–50; Chapter 4 §§4.1–4.3, printed pp. 57–66; Chapter 5 §§5.1–5.4, printed pp. 69–92.

contents.name: §3.1, Overlapping versus Non-overlapping Methods
contents.reason: The assigned pair proves a finite-dimensional SPD subspace-correction theory and a cube-mesh example; the section’s transmission-problem comparison is not asserted.

contents.name: §3.2, Overlapping Schwarz Methods with Many Subdomains
contents.reason: The data definition and two-level P1 theorem state their own local spaces, residual restrictions, coarse space, and overlap geometry.

contents.name: §3.3, Discrete Variational Formulation of Schwarz Methods
contents.reason: The local matrices are derived from the restricted energy form, and the carrier verifies symmetry, positive definiteness, and unique local solves.

contents.name: §3.4, Coarse Grid Correction
contents.reason: The definition uses the Galerkin coarse matrix and cites the actual Galerkin projector supplier with matching SPD and rank hypotheses.

contents.name: §4.1, Subspace Correction Methods
contents.reason: The local correction proof verifies idempotence, energy self-adjointness, range, and the Pythagorean identity.

contents.name: §4.2, Additive Case, Lemmas 4.5 and 4.7 and Theorem 4.8
contents.reason: The carrier proves the exact additive Rayleigh bounds and inexact-solver spectral-equivalence factor under explicit constants.

contents.name: §4.3, Multiplicative Case, Theorem 4.10
contents.reason: The carrier proves a coarse-first exact-sweep contraction using ordered corrections and does not assume commuting projections.

contents.name: §5.1, Technical Preliminaries: Friedrich, Poincare, and scaled trace estimates
contents.reason: The structured proof uses its explicitly stated Scott–Zhang estimate and a direct support count; these separate boundary-layer estimates are not invoked.

contents.name: §5.2, Coarse Grid Contribution, Definition 5.4 and Lemmas 5.5–5.6
contents.reason: The source gives a related coarse-interpolation stable split; this carrier independently uses the inspected Scott–Zhang supplier and proves its stated H-overlap bound.

contents.name: §5.3, Lemma 5.7 on P2-to-P1 interpolation energy stability
contents.reason: The product of two affine functions is P2; the local lemma proves the sharper weighted gradient estimate needed for the cutoff product.

contents.name: §5.3, Lemma 5.8 on a subdomain boundary layer
contents.reason: The local proof bounds the number of padded cube supports directly and does not use a boundary-layer Poincare estimate.

contents.name: §5.3, Assumptions 5.9–5.10 and Lemma 5.11 (partition of unity)
contents.reason: The local proof constructs a distance-based partition, proves its denominator and gradient bounds, and verifies bounded support overlap.

contents.name: §5.4, Lemma 5.12 on the additive upper bound
contents.reason: The combined theorem proves its own support-count synthesis bound C1=1+7^d and the pairwise overlap matrix norm rho≤11^d.

contents.name: §5.4, Lemma 5.13 stable splitting for two-level overlapping Schwarz
contents.reason: The source theorem has related quasi-uniformity and subdomain assumptions and yields a stable split; the local carrier proves the weaker explicit 1+(H/delta)^2 bound for its structured family.
